name: hmmscan with Pfam
compares: Each query protein against the curated profile models of every Pfam family, without searching any relative.
score: Domain bit score: higher ranks first. E-value cutoffs 10 (sequence and domain).
failure_modes: Pfam domains are defined by these same models, so scoring hmmscan against the Pfam truth set grades the models against their own output. Read its Pfam row as the best a search could do, not as a competitor.
It was scored against the Pfam truth set only. Swiss-Prot features and Pfam-N: not run.
licence: BSD 3-clause (HMMER); CC0 1.0 (Pfam-A models, per the Pfam 38.2 release notes)

source.node_from: sacct -u olgabot -X -n -P -S 2026-08-31 -E 2026-09-14 --format=JobID,NodeList,Partition,AllocTRES, matched on the trace's native_id
source.hardware_from: scontrol -o show node <node>: AvailableFeatures CPU_MNF, CPU_SKU, GPU_SKU

questions: Is every family you expect to find already in Pfam? If no, this tool cannot find it: it only reports families that have a Pfam model.

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.785 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.802 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.871 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.580 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.573 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, no relative searched, setting `direct`.)
Can you spend about 0.389 core-hours per 1,000 proteins? That is the measured cost of scanning them against Pfam's models.
